mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.2 percentage points, expected S&P 500 20-day forward returns turn positive due to reduced discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-positive despite FEDFUNDS increase, or the increase is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (employment) above 140,000 suggests labor market strength, which is associated with higher corporate earnings expectations and positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative when PAYEMS crosses above 140,000 without subsequent earnings beat expectations.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in HOUST (retail sales) of over 2% indicates weakening consumer demand, which predicts negative S&P 20-day forward returns as investors anticipate lower corporate profits.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite a larger than 2% drop in HOUST, or the effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly INDPRO index below 103.0 (2017=100) signals supply-side constraints, leading to higher S&P 20-day forward returns as relative scarcity boosts equity valuations.
failure_condition: INDPRO remains above 103.0 with no positive 20-day forward returns, or the effect is not robust across multiple cycles.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 5.5% for three consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be positive due to lower real borrowing costs and increased equity valuation.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day return when UNRATE meets the trigger, or the effect is spurious (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) exceeding 1% each suggest dual demand weakness, resulting in negative S&P 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive despite both proxies falling by >1%, or interaction is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE rises above 7%, the S&P 20-day forward return turns negative due to higher wage growth depressing real wage expectations and corporate profit margins.
failure_condition: Forward returns are positive when UNRATE crosses above 7%, or the effect is not robust across multiple cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 2% suggests disinflation, which is associated with positive S&P 60-day forward returns as investors price in lower future discount rates.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative despite CPIAUCSL meeting the trigger, or the effect is not statistically significant.
